01

Context is the foundation

One home for the facts your team and agents use. These example briefs are ready to replace with your own.

⌘

Context

The shared operating manual.

↗OfferThe promise, deliverables, and boundaries.→↗PositioningWhat makes your approach worth choosing.→↗Ideal customerWho you serve and who you do not.→↗Sales processA repeatable path from first contact to delivery.→↗Voice & toneHow your team sounds in every conversation.→↗Operating rulesOwnership, thresholds, and review cadence.→
← Context

Offer

The promise, deliverables, and boundaries.

Example brief

  • A four-week operating system pilot.
  • Map one workflow, agree on success criteria, build the smallest useful system, and review adoption.
  • A clear scope and named owner are required before delivery.
← Context

Positioning

What makes your approach worth choosing.

Example brief

  • Make useful work easier to repeat.
  • Connect shared knowledge to everyday decisions and remove manual handoffs.
  • Show a concrete before-and-after instead of promising universal automation.
← Context

Ideal customer

Who you serve and who you do not.

Example brief

  • Teams of 10–50 with a repeatable service workflow.
  • A decision owner, one measurable bottleneck, and time for a small pilot.
  • Avoid projects without a clear owner or a realistic success measure.
← Context

Sales process

A repeatable path from first contact to delivery.

Example brief

  • Discover → qualify → propose → agree → deliver.
  • Every stage has an owner, evidence, and a next step.
  • Review the forecast weekly and archive stalled opportunities deliberately.
← Context

Voice & tone

How your team sounds in every conversation.

Example brief

  • Clear, warm, and specific.
  • Lead with the customer’s situation, explain the next step, and keep promises bounded.
  • Use examples. Avoid hype, pressure, and unsupported outcomes.
← Context

Operating rules

Ownership, thresholds, and review cadence.

Example brief

  • Review pipeline every Friday.
  • Require human review before messages, proposals, contracts, or external actions.
  • Use permission-checked vault reads when connecting this template to real data.

Capabilities

Playbooks to customize with your agent

Call preparation

Review the account, last conversation, open questions, and next decision.

Follow-up draft

Write a concise recap with an owner and date for every next step.

Pipeline review

Summarize changes, close-date risks, and opportunities needing attention.

Proposal outline

Translate agreed scope into outcomes, milestones, and acceptance criteria.

Account research

Build a sourced account brief from documents you can access.

Win / loss review

Capture what changed the outcome and improve the next conversation.
